title: How does a credit card payment happen in seconds?

lines.text: When you tap your credit card at a store register, the payment approves in under two seconds.
lines.caps: What happens when | you *tap your | *credit card?

lines.text: In those two seconds, your data embarks on a worldwide journey across thousands of miles of fiber optics.
lines.caps: Your data races *thousands | of miles across | *undersea fiber

lines.text: The card's microchip generates a one-time cryptographic token to prevent fraud.
The terminal beams this token to the merchant's bank, which routes it through Visa or Mastercard's global network.
lines.caps: Beams data to *Visa | or Mastercard's global | *supercomputers

lines.text: Their supercomputers check for fraud algorithms, then ping your personal bank to verify your funds.
lines.caps: Pings your *bank | to check funds and *fraud

lines.text: Your bank approves the charge, transmits the confirmation code back, and the register beeps approved.
All of that happened in less time than it took you to blink twice.
lines.caps: Happened in *less time | than a single *blink!
